items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We also made friends with a couple of Egyptian military aviators

ctx.x: A.J. Henderson, known as "Ginger" because of his red hair, played trumpet and Teddy Hill was a drummer. The other two, Henry Campbell and Nick something, were just pals of Ginger. Henry Campbell played tenor-sax. They loved our music. Ginger was not a jazz trumpet player but Teddy Hill was the best drummer in Egypt and we really enjoyed when he would come around and sit in with us. There were many bands in Europe and the U.S.A. that would have been happy to have him as a drummer. We invited Ginger to sit in also…

We also made friends with a couple of Egyptian military aviators and some coast guards officers. After we became well acquainted with the coast guards officers, they used to give us big pieces of hashish and told us how they got it. There was plenty of hashish smoking in Egypt. Women were not allowed in Egyptian bars of sidewalk cafes. But everywhere, but I never found out if there was a law against it or only a law against smuggling because these coast guard officers told us that whenever they caught someone…

We had a band valet whose name was Hassan but we called him Sam. In return he had a name for each of us because some of the names were too difficult for him. I was Gee-Gee, Burns was Mr. Eat for what reason I don't know, because Burns was not a big eater. Edgar Courance was Auspa. I don't remember the names he gave to the others.
